items.title: EU presses OpenAI, Anthropic for more details on AI safety incidents
items.excerpt: The European Commission has sent OpenAI and Anthropic questions under the AI Act's general-purpose model rules: how many safety incidents happened, where the EU was affected, and how they changed risk assessment and security practices. Published time verified via r.jina.ai (site is Cloudflare-blocked).

history_match.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents

items.title: Norway suspends electricity grid access for new data centres
items.excerpt: Norway's grid operator Statnett suspended new data centre connection applications for a year. The government says it will use the pause to build a data centre licensing scheme and consider state ownership, amid concern over the AI industry's power demand. Time verified via r.jina.ai.

items.title: EU countries still can't get it together on AI
items.excerpt: Ahead of the Dublin leaders' meeting on AI (Nov 13), 16 capitals have missed the deadline to appoint a national authority to enforce the AI Act, and Brussels has delayed data centre support because of national administrative holdups. The Commission confirmed the count.
items.axis: policy / EU AI Act national enforcement

items.title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem
items.excerpt: Nvidia's board is investigating whether Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang through an affair he has admitted. This follows the House GOP chairs' Megaspeed briefing request (covered 11-07). Running story: the new elements are Nvidia's formal board probe and Huang's memo; skip if the curator treats it as re-reporting.
items.axis: geopolitics / US-China AI chips, national security

history_match.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns

items.title: Trump's 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
items.excerpt: In a 60 Minutes interview, President Trump said 'I don't mind guardrails' for AI, a shift from his earlier preference for industry self-policing, and threatened to arrest an AI executive. Attribute all claims to Trump. It is a statement, not a document.

items.title: The global pledge to use AI for climate good is a cruel joke
items.excerpt: An opinion-style analysis of the AI-for-climate pledge launched at the UN COP31 talks in Antalya. It argues the pledge leaves AI data centres' own energy and emissions footprint largely unaddressed. The underlying pledge is an intergovernmental document.
items.axis: geopolitics / AI datacenters, UN climate diplomacy

items.title: Revealed: Palantir lobbied minister to stretch AI tools' reach to NHS GP records
items.excerpt: WhatsApp messages seen by the Guardian show Palantir pressing health minister Zubir Ahmed to help bring sensitive GP record data into its NHS AI platform.
items.axis: policy / AI procurement and health data privacy (UK)

items.title: Parents and teachers decry Google pledge to yank Search if schools block AI
items.excerpt: Google says schools should control student AI use, but schools that block its AI tools will lose access to its search engine. Parents and teachers called the policy 'extortion'.
items.axis: policy / platform AI policy in schools

items.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence
items.excerpt: CSET previews a forthcoming study. The US leads in frontier models and compute, while China pursues broader paths to AGI, including robotics, embodiment and brain-inspired systems. The study asks what US policymakers should do.

items.title: Chinese AI firms want Silicon Valley's top minds. Poaching them won't be easy
items.excerpt: MiniMax and Moonshot are setting up US outposts to hire engineers. Pay gaps, weaker prestige and national-security tensions make it hard to lure talent away from OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: PM call with President Macron of France: 9 November 2026
items.excerpt: The UK Prime Minister joined a Macron-chaired leaders' call on AI. He said AI will top the agenda of the UK's 2027 G20 presidency, that the UK will advance international AI standards, and that the AI Security Institute's expertise is available. This is the primary government readout.

items.title: Freedom House Charts 'Seismic Shifts' on the Global Internet
items.excerpt: A podcast discussion with experts after the release of Freedom House's annual Freedom on the Net report, including how governments use AI for censorship, surveillance and online manipulation. The primary document is the Freedom House report.
items.axis: elections & public opinion / AI-enabled censorship and manipulation

items.title: AI 안경 쓰고 시험 치다 적발된 중·고생 4명…전원 0점 처리
items.excerpt: 교육부는 전국 중·고교를 대상으로 스마트 안경 내신평가 부정행위를 전수조사해 4건(중1·고3)을 확인했다. 적발된 학생은 모두 0점 처리됐다. 11-08 수능 스마트안경 카드의 후속으로, 공식 조사 결과와 처분이라는 새 사실이 있다.
items.axis: policy / government enforcement on AI devices (Korea)

items.title: [단독] AI 시대 교육 '백년지대계' 연구 예산 전액 삭감
items.excerpt: 정부 2027년도 예산안에서 교육부 '국가AI교육연구센터' 설립·운용 예산 30억원이 빠진 채 국회에 제출됐다. 업계와 학계는 원상복구를 요구하고 있다. 국회 예산 심사 단계의 사안이다.

items.title: 국방 AI 선도연구기관에 카이스트·ETRI·LG AI연구원 지정
items.excerpt: 방위사업청이 국방 인공지능(AI) 분야 선도연구기관으로 KAIST, ETRI, LG AI연구원을 지정했다.

items.title: 배경훈, ITU서 한국 AI 비전 제시…이사국 10선 도전
items.excerpt: 배경훈 부총리 겸 과기정통부 장관이 국제전기통신연합(ITU) 전권회의에서 한국의 AI·디지털 정책 비전을 제시했다. 정부 발표이지만 정책 신호는 약하다.

items.title: Deepfake Penalties Rejected 20–15
items.excerpt: Bahrain's Shura Council voted 20–15 to reject a bill with criminal penalties for deepfake misuse, amid debate sparked by a fake video of a Shura member. Off-list outlet: none of the allowed outlets carried this legislative vote.

items.title: Erwin Tulfo files bill seeking worker protection vs. layoffs due to AI
items.excerpt: Philippine Senator Erwin Tulfo filed Senate Bill 2563 to amend the Labor Code. Before AI-driven layoffs, employers would have to give six months' notice to DOLE and workers and offer reskilling and higher separation pay. Off-list outlet: it covers a bill filing not carried by the allowed outlets.
